name: SenideOG
tagline: Builds a species x orthogroup matrix from scratch with OrthoFinder, as an alternative to the GO-term matrix.
what_for: The GO-term unit is biased: terms are transferred by embedding similarity, so species with well-annotated relatives look richer than they are. SenideOG replaces that unit with orthogroups inferred from the sequences themselves. Eight modules: inventory the proteomes, normalise them to one isoform per gene, QC them with BUSCO, pick a core of about 64 species stratified by order and family, run OrthoFinder de novo on that core, assign the remaining species to those orthogroups, build the species x orthogroup matrix in the same shape as the GO matrix, and annotate each orthogroup with a GO consensus.

inputs.name: Proteomes
inputs.description: The FANTASIA_project tree, or a flat folder with one proteome FASTA per species.

inputs.name: Core size
inputs.description: Species in the de novo OrthoFinder run (default 64).

inputs.name: Matrix filter
inputs.description: Drop orthogroups present in fewer than this many species (default 4).

outputs.description: Species x orthogroup counts, the same shape as the GO-term matrix so both can be compared.
BUSCO completeness and FASTA-to-GO id match rate per species.
GO consensus and description per orthogroup.

requirements.notes: About 300 GB of disk for the core all-vs-all and the gene trees; superseded in practice by the SonicParanoid run.
